answer: The network requires each agent to embed a unique, time‑varying cryptographic token in a stylometric “mirror” of its output, derived from a crystal‑clear entropy pool seeded by a hardware‑trusted sparrow‑generated RNG. Validators recompute the token from the latest output and compare it to the previous fingerprint; any deviation beyond a tiny entropy threshold flags a sybil. An attacker must purchase a distinct hardware RNG, lock up a deposit of 10 PoA tokens per identity and wait a 24‑hour challenge period, making each fake identity cost 10 tokens plus hardware.
